title: Rigveda 9.31: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.31: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.31 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 679r-679v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.31.1-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 679v
translation.original_text:
1pra somā̍saḥ svā̱dhya1̱̍ḥ pava̍mānāso akramuḥ | ra̱yiṁ kṛ̍ṇvanti̱ ceta̍nam ||
2di̱vas pṛ̍thi̱vyā adhi̱ bhave̍ndo dyumna̱vardha̍naḥ | bhavā̱ vājā̍nā̱m pati̍ḥ ||
3tubhya̱ṁ vātā̍ abhi̱priya̱s tubhya̍m arṣanti̱ sindha̍vaḥ | soma̱ vardha̍nti te̱ maha̍ḥ ||
4ā pyā̍yasva̱ sam e̍tu te vi̱śvata̍ḥ soma̱ vṛṣṇya̍m | bhavā̱ vāja̍sya saṁga̱the ||
5tubhya̱ṁ gāvo̍ ghṛ̱tam payo̱ babhro̍ dudu̱hre akṣi̍tam | varṣi̍ṣṭhe̱ adhi̱ sāna̍vi ||
6svā̱yu̱dhasya̍ te sa̱to bhuva̍nasya pate va̱yam | indo̍ sakhi̱tvam u̍śmasi ||
translation.text:
1THE, Soma-drops, benevolent, come forth as they are purified, Bestowing wealth which all may see.
2O Indu, high o'er heaven and earth be thou, increaser of our might: The Master of all strength be thou.
3The winds are gracious in their love to thee, the rivers flow to thee Soma, they multiply thy power.
4Soma, wax great. From every side may vigorous powers unite in thee: Be in the gathering-Place of strength.
5For thee, brown-hued! the kine have poured imperishable oil and milk. Aloft on the sublimest height.
6Friendship, O Indu, we desire with thee who bearest noble arms, With thee, O Lord of all that is.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 679v (numbered 101v by the scribe) (OPenn image 680, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.31.1 ‹svādhyaḥ pavamānāsaḥ akramuḥ rayim›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 680r (numbered 102r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.32.5 ‹yathā hitam›. Verses 9.31.1-6 end on this page; 9.31.1 begins on fol. 679r (numbered 101r by the scribe).
